author: Eustathius of Antioch
occasion: The fragments preserve Eustathius's arguments on the incarnation and on the universal care of the catholic Church, likely from anti-Arian or pastoral contexts.
argument: Eustathius argues that the one who appeared on earth and lived among human beings is not only human but also God, as Jeremiah the prophet says. He insists that this divine figure was born with human beings from a virgin, shared infancy, growth, food, and drink, and thus truly shared human life. He also argues that if prayers must be made for the catholic Church throughout the whole world, then all the more must providential care be shown for the whole Church, with equal concern for all its parts.

outline.move: The fragments present two arguments: first, that the one who appeared on earth is both God and human, sharing fully in human life from the virgin birth onward; second, that the Church's universal scope demands universal providential care.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Jacob... called his child (τῶι παιδὶ αὐτοῦ = his child/servant)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν Ἰακὼβ τῶι παιδὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ Ἰσραὴλ τῶι ἠγαπημένωι ὑπ' αὐτοῦ
_unresolved_facts.fix: Jacob is the recipient ('to Jacob'), not the one whose child is mentioned. The phrase τῶι παιδὶ αὐτοῦ refers to God's child/servant, not Jacob's. The structure is: 'he gave it to Jacob, to his [God's] child, and to Israel the beloved by him [God].' Jacob and Israel are likely identified as the same figure (Jacob/Israel the patriarch), both recipients, with τῶι παιδὶ αὐτοῦ being in apposition to Ἰακὼβ or referring to a messianic figure.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Israel... mentioned alongside Jacob as a distinct recipient figure in the quotation
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν Ἰακὼβ τῶι παιδὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ Ἰσραὴλ τῶι ἠγαπημένωι ὑπ' αὐτοῦ
_unresolved_facts.fix: Israel may be the same person as Jacob (the patriarch with the dual name Jacob/Israel), not necessarily a distinct figure. The brief should note the ambiguity: Jacob and Israel could be two names for one patriarch, or two distinct figures.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: καθὼς καὶ Ἱερεμίας ὁ προφήτης λέγει
_unresolved_facts.fix: Jeremiah is only quoted in frag-open and frag-rem-early. The quotation from Jeremiah ends after 'οὐ λογισθήσεται ἕτερος πρὸς αὐτόν.' The material in frag-rem-mid ('Ἐξεῦρε πᾶσαν ὁδὸν...') is not marked as Jeremiah's speech; it appears to be Eustathius's continuation or another quotation not attributed to Jeremiah. Sections should be ['frag-open', 'frag-rem-early'].

_unresolved_facts.claim: He insists that this divine figure was born with human beings from a virgin
_unresolved_facts.fix: The Greek says 'was born together with them [human beings] from a virgin' (συνεγεννήθη μετ' αὐτῶν ἐκ παρθένου), not 'born with human beings from a virgin.' The 'with' (μετ' αὐτῶν) refers to being born alongside other human beings, sharing in human birth; 'from a virgin' specifies the manner of his birth. The brief's wording is awkward and potentially misleading about the syntax.
